means: Visible brushwork - shading made of strokes with direction and edge rather than of flat regions. The opposite pole from cel logic.
does: Abandons the hard terminator entirely: shadows blend, edges soften, and brush texture appears in skin, cloth and background. The tested clause is 'painterly shading, visible brushstrokes' and it genuinely moves the picture. But it fights the house style of every film here - the moment it lands, cel shading stops being the thing you are looking at.
reach_for_it: backgrounds, and memory or dream beats where you want the frame to stop looking animated. Scope it to the background via anime.bg.style rather than the whole frame, or the characters go soft with it.
used_in: anime.draw.shading_steps/painterly, and as an axis of anime.bg.style
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short dark hair, plain jacket, standing, city street, daytime
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
